translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Sales Field received surplus goods from within and without, calculated value to await sale, or approved offset disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Sales Field received surplus goods from across the empire, priced them for sale, or approved them for offset disbursement.

sentences.zh: 榷貨務，掌折博斛斗、金帛之屬。

translations.literal: The Monopoly Goods Office managed exchange of grain measures, gold, silk, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The Monopoly Goods Office handled exchange of grain, gold, silk, and related goods.

sentences.zh: 交引庫，掌給印出納交引錢鈔之事。

translations.literal: The Exchange Note Store managed printing and receipt and disbursement of exchange notes and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The Exchange Note Store printed and managed the issue and redemption of exchange notes and paper money.

sentences.zh: 抵當所，掌以官錢聽民質取而濟其緩急。

translations.literal: The Pawn Office used official funds to allow the people to pawn goods and relieve their urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: The Pawn Office lent official funds against pledges to relieve public hardship.

sentences.zh: 和劑局、惠民局，掌修合良藥，出賣以濟民疾。

translations.literal: The Compounding Bureau and the Beneficent Bureau compounded fine medicines and sold them to relieve the people's illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: The Compounding Bureau and the Beneficent Bureau compounded medicines and sold them to treat public illness.

sentences.zh: 店宅務，掌管官屋及邸店，計置出僦及修造之事。

translations.literal: The Shops and Residences Office managed government buildings and inns, arranging rental and repair.
translations.idiomatic: The Shops and Residences Office managed government buildings and shops, handling rentals and repairs.

sentences.zh: 石炭場，掌受納出賣石炭。

translations.literal: The Coal Yard received, stored, and sold coal.
translations.idiomatic: The Coal Yard received and sold coal.

sentences.zh: 香藥庫，掌出納外國貢獻及市舶香藥、寶石之事。

translations.literal: The Spices and Drugs Store managed receipt and disbursement of foreign tribute and maritime-trade spices, drugs, and gems.
translations.idiomatic: The Spices and Drugs Store managed foreign tribute and maritime spices, drugs, and gems.

sentences.zh: 建炎詔罷太府寺，以其所掌職務撥隸金部。

translations.literal: In Jianyan an edict abolished the Court of the Imperial Treasury and transferred its duties to the Gold Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1127 an edict abolished the Court of the Imperial Treasury and transferred its functions to the Gold Bureau.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，復以章億守太府寺丞，措置印給茶鹽鈔引，續添置丞二員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, Zhang Yi was again appointed to serve as assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury to arrange printing and issuance of tea and salt note certificates; two assistant posts were subsequently added.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 Zhang Yi was again appointed assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury to organize printing and issuance of tea and salt notes, and two more assistant posts were added.

sentences.zh: 四年，復置卿、少各一員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, one director and one vice-director were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134 the director and vice-director were restored.

sentences.zh: 十年，復置主簿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the registrar was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1140 the registrar post was restored.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔交引庫書押鈔引寺丞兩員。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ordered two assistant directors of the court to sign and seal note certificates at the Exchange Note Store.
translations.idiomatic: In 1141 an edict assigned two court assistant directors to sign note certificates at the Exchange Note Store.

sentences.zh: 遇合推賞。

translations.literal: When promotions were recommended,
translations.idiomatic: When promotions were recommended,

sentences.zh: 各與減磨勘二年。

translations.literal: each received a two-year reduction in tenure review.
translations.idiomatic: each received a two-year reduction in tenure review.

sentences.zh: 尋詔三丞一體行之。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered all three assistants to receive this equally.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon extended the same benefit to all three assistants.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，並省主簿一員，明年如舊制，設案七，以序次分管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, one registrar post was cut in consolidation; the next year the old system was restored and seven case sections were established for sequential division of duties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1163 one registrar post was cut; the following year the former staffing was restored with seven case sections dividing duties in order.

sentences.zh: 監交案，隨逐丞簿赴左藏庫監交看驗綱運錢物。

translations.literal: The Supervised Handover Section accompanied assistants and registrars to the Left Treasury stores to supervise handover and inspect cord-transported funds and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervised Handover Section accompanied assistants and registrars to the Left Treasury to inspect incoming cord shipments of funds and goods.

sentences.zh: 中興後，所隸惟有糧料院、審計司、左藏東西庫、交引庫、祗候庫、和劑局、惠民局如前製所置。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, subordinate offices were only the Grain Rations Office, Audit Office, Eastern and Western Left Treasury stores, Exchange Note Store, Attendant Service Store, Compounding Bureau, and Beneficent Bureau, established as in the former system.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration its subordinates were only the Grain Rations Office, Audit Office, Eastern and Western Left Treasury stores, Exchange Note Store, Attendant Service Store, and the Compounding and Beneficent Bureaus, as under the earlier system.

sentences.zh: 左藏南庫，

translations.literal: The Left Treasury Southern Store,
translations.idiomatic: The Left Treasury Southern Store,

translations.literal: (sealed reserve)
translations.idiomatic: (sealed reserve)

sentences.zh: 管御前激賞庫改。

translations.literal: was changed from managing the Imperial Reward Store.
translations.idiomatic: was renamed from the Imperial Reward Store.

sentences.zh: 以侍從官提領，又置提轄檢察官一員，編估局、打套局，

translations.literal: It was led by an attendant official, and one inspector-in-charge was also established, together with the Appraisal Bureau and the Packing Bureau,
translations.idiomatic: It was led by an attendant official, with an inspector-in-charge and the Appraisal Bureau and Packing Bureau,

sentences.zh: 〈（二局係揀選市舶香藥雜物等第，會其直以待貿易。）〉

translations.literal: (The two bureaus sorted maritime-trade spices, drugs, and miscellaneous goods by grade and assessed their value to await trade.)
translations.idiomatic: (The two bureaus graded maritime spices and miscellaneous goods and assessed their value for trade.)

sentences.zh: 寄樁庫，掌發賣香藥、匹帛，拘其直歸於左藏南庫。

translations.literal: The Deposited Reserve Store sold spices and drugs and bolts of silk and cloth, collecting payment and returning it to the Left Treasury Southern Store.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposited Reserve Store sold spices and silk, remitting the proceeds to the Left Treasury Southern Store.

sentences.zh: 置監官提領二人。

translations.literal: Two supervising officials were established to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising officials were appointed to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 【國子監】舊置判監事二人，以兩製或帶職朝官充，凡監事皆總之。

translations.literal: 【Imperial Academy】 Formerly two chief commissioners were established, filled by edict drafters or incumbent capital officials; all directorate affairs were overseen by them.
translations.idiomatic: 【Imperial Academy】 The academy formerly had two chief commissioners, filled by edict drafters or incumbent capital officials, who oversaw all directorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 直講八人，以京官、選人充，掌以經術教授諸生，

translations.literal: Eight lecturers-in-chief, filled by capital officials and selectees, lectured students in classical learning,
translations.idiomatic: Eight lecturers-in-chief, drawn from capital officials and selectees, taught students the classics,

sentences.zh: 〈（舊以講書為名，無定員。

translations.literal: (Formerly called lecturers on books, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: (They had formerly been called lecturers on books, with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，判監李至奏為直講，以京朝官充。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Chief Commissioner Li Zhi memorialized to rename the post lecturer-in-chief, filled by capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 994 Chief Commissioner Li Zhi memorialized to rename the post lecturer-in-chief and fill it with capital officials.

sentences.zh: 其後，又有講書、說書之名，並以幕職、州縣官充。

translations.literal: Later there were also the titles lecturer on books and expounder on books, both filled by staff officials and prefecture and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later the titles lecturer on books and expounder on books also appeared, filled by staff and local officials.

sentences.zh: 其熟於講說而秩滿者，稍遷京官。

translations.literal: Those skilled in lecturing who completed their terms were gradually promoted to capital official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those skilled in lecturing who completed their terms were gradually promoted to capital official rank.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，始以八人為額，每員各專一經，並選擇進士並《九經》及第之人，相參薦舉。）〉

translations.literal: In Huangyou the quota was first fixed at eight; each post specialized in one classic, and jinshi and 《Nine Classics》 degree holders were selected and jointly recommended.)
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou the quota was fixed at eight, each lecturer specializing in one classic and chosen from jinshi and 《Nine Classics》 graduates by joint recommendation.)

sentences.zh: 丞一人，以京朝官或選人充，掌錢穀出納之事。

translations.literal: One assistant, filled by a capital official or selectee, managed receipt and disbursement of funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant, drawn from capital officials or selectees, managed receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，以京官或選人充，掌文簿以勾考其出納。

translations.literal: One registrar, filled by a capital official or selectee, kept records to audit receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: One registrar, drawn from capital officials or selectees, kept records and audited receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 〈（舊制，祭酒闕，始置判監事。）〉

translations.literal: (Under the old system, when the Director was vacant, chief commissioners were first established.)
translations.idiomatic: (Under the old system, chief commissioners were established only when the Director's post was vacant.)

sentences.zh: 監生無定員。

translations.literal: Directorate students had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 〈（並有蔭及京畿人，初隸監授業，後補監生；

translations.literal: (There were those with hereditary privilege and natives of the capital region; at first they were attached to the directorate for instruction and later enrolled as students;
translations.idiomatic: (Some held hereditary privilege or came from the capital region; they first studied at the directorate and were later enrolled as students;

sentences.zh: 或隨屬遊官，以久離本貫，不克赴鄉薦，而文藝可稱，亦許隸補試。

translations.literal: or traveling officials long absent from their native place who could not attend local recommendations but whose literary accomplishment was commendable were also permitted to attach and take trial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: traveling officials long absent from home who could not seek local recommendation but showed literary promise were also permitted to enroll and take trial examinations.

sentences.zh: 廣文教進士，太學教《九經》、《五經、》《三禮》、《三傳》學究，律學館教明律，餘不常置。）〉

translations.literal: Broad Learning taught jinshi; the Imperial College taught 《Nine Classics》, 《Five Classics》, 《Three Rites》, and 《Three Commentaries》 classicists; the Law Institute taught statutory law; the rest were not regularly established.)
translations.idiomatic: Broad Learning instructed jinshi candidates; the Imperial College taught 《Nine Classics》, 《Five Classics》, 《Three Rites》, and 《Three Commentaries》 specialists; the Law Institute taught statutory law; other schools were not regularly maintained.)

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，始置察酒、司業、丞、主簿各一人，太學博士十人，

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng bureaucratic system was implemented, one Director, one Vice-Director, one assistant, and one registrar were first established, together with ten Imperial College doctors,
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuanfeng reforms, one Director, one Vice-Director, one assistant, and one registrar were established, along with ten Imperial College doctors,

sentences.zh: 〈（舊係國子監直講，元豐三年，詔改為太學博士，每經二人。）〉

translations.literal: (Formerly Imperial Academy lecturers-in-chief; in the third year of Yuanfeng an edict changed them to Imperial College doctors, two for each classic.)
translations.idiomatic: (Formerly Imperial Academy lecturers-in-chief; in 1080 an edict renamed them Imperial College doctors, with two assigned to each classic.)

sentences.zh: 正、錄各五人，武學博士二人，律學博士、正各一人。

translations.literal: Five rectifiers and five registrars each, two Military College doctors, and one Law College doctor and one rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: There were five rectifiers and five registrars, two Military College doctors, and one Law College doctor and one rectifier.

sentences.zh: 【祭酒】掌國子、太學、武學、律學、小學之政令，司業為之貳，丞參領監事。

translations.literal: 【Director of the Directorate】 Managed policies for the Directorate, Imperial College, Military College, Law College, and Primary School; the Vice-Director was second to him, and the assistant shared in overseeing directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 【Director of the Directorate】 The Director managed the Directorate, Imperial College, Military College, Law College, and Primary School. The Vice-Director assisted him, and the assistant shared administrative oversight.

sentences.zh: 凡諸生之隸於太學者，分三舍。

translations.literal: All students attached to the Imperial College were divided into three dormitories.
translations.idiomatic: Students attached to the Imperial College were divided into three dormitories.

sentences.zh: 始入學，驗所隸州公據，以試補中者充外舍。

translations.literal: On first entering, their credentials from the state to which they were attached were verified; those who passed the trial placement examination became outer-dormitory students.
translations.idiomatic: On entry, students verified their state credentials; those who passed the placement examination entered the outer dormitory.

sentences.zh: 齊長、諭月書其行藝於籍。

translations.literal: Dormitory heads and instructors monthly recorded conduct and learning in the register.
translations.idiomatic: Dormitory heads and instructors recorded each student's conduct and academic performance monthly.

sentences.zh: 行謂率教不戾規矩，藝謂治經程文，季終考於學諭，次學錄，次學正，次博士，然後考於長貳。

translations.literal: Conduct meant following instruction without violating rules; learning meant classical essays; at quarter's end they were examined by the instructor, then the registrar, then the rectifier, then the doctor, and finally by the chief and vice.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct meant obeying school rules; learning meant classical composition. Each quarter students were examined by the instructor, registrar, rectifier, and doctor, and finally by the chief and vice directors.

sentences.zh: 歲終校定，具注於籍以俟覆試，視其校定之數，參驗而序進之。

translations.literal: At year's end evaluations were finalized and fully entered in the register to await re-examination; viewing the evaluation numbers, they were cross-checked and advanced in order.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end evaluations were recorded in the register pending re-examination, and students were promoted in order according to their scores.

sentences.zh: 凡私試，孟月經義，仲月論，季月策。

translations.literal: For private examinations, the first month tested classical meaning, the second month discourse, and the third month policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Private examinations tested classical interpretation in the first month, discourse in the second, and policy questions in the third.

sentences.zh: 公試，初場以經義，次場以論、策。

translations.literal: For public examinations, the first session tested classical meaning and the second session discourse and policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Public examinations tested classical interpretation in the first session and discourse and policy questions in the second.

sentences.zh: 試上舍如省試法。

translations.literal: Examination of the upper dormitory followed the provincial examination method.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-dormitory examinations followed provincial examination rules.

sentences.zh: 凡內舍行藝與所試之等俱優者，為上舍上等，取旨命官；

translations.literal: When inner-dormitory conduct and learning together with examination rank were all excellent, this was upper upper-dormitory rank, and imperial appointment followed;
translations.idiomatic: Inner-dormitory students with excellent conduct, learning, and examination scores ranked in the upper dormitory and received direct imperial appointment;

sentences.zh: 一優一平為中，以俟殿試；

translations.literal: one excellent and one average was middle rank, awaiting the palace examination;
translations.idiomatic: one excellent and one average score placed a student in the middle rank, eligible for the palace examination;

sentences.zh: 一優一否或俱平為下，以俟省試。

translations.literal: one excellent and one failing, or both average, was lower rank, awaiting the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: one excellent and one failing score, or both average, placed a student in the lower rank, eligible for the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 唯國子生不預考選。

translations.literal: Only Directorate students did not participate in examination selection.
translations.idiomatic: Only Directorate students were exempt from the examination selection process.

sentences.zh: 凡課試、升黜、教導之事，長、貳皆總焉。

translations.literal: All matters of examinations, promotion and demotion, and instruction were overseen by the chief and vice.
translations.idiomatic: The chief and vice directors oversaw examinations, promotions and demotions, and instruction.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸學，則率官屬諸生班迎，即行在距學百步亦如之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the academy, they led officials and students in formation to welcome it; the same was done when the temporary residence was one hundred paces from the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the academy, the Director led officials and students in formal welcome; the same ceremony was observed when the imperial residence was within one hundred paces of the academy.

sentences.zh: 凡釋奠於先聖、先師及武成王，則率官屬諸生共薦獻之禮。

translations.literal: For offerings to the Sage, former teachers, and the Martial Accomplishment King, they led officials and students jointly in presentation rites.
translations.idiomatic: For offerings to the Sage, former teachers, and the Martial Accomplishment King, the Director led officials and students in the joint presentation rites.

sentences.zh: 歲計所隸三舍生升降多寡之數，以為學官之殿最賞罰。

translations.literal: At year's end they calculated numbers of promoted and demoted students in the three dormitories under their jurisdiction as the basis for merit evaluation, rewards, and punishments of school officials.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the numbers of promotions and demotions among the three dormitories determined school officials' merit ratings and rewards or punishments.

sentences.zh: 博士，掌分經講授，考校程文，以德行道藝訓導學者。

translations.literal: Doctors divided the classics for lecturing, examined essays, and instructed learners in virtue, conduct, and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Doctors lectured on assigned classics, graded essays, and instructed students in virtue, conduct, and scholarship.

sentences.zh: 正、錄，掌舉行學規，凡諸生之戾規矩者，待以五等之罰，考校訓導如博士之職。

translations.literal: Rectifiers and registrars enforced school regulations; for students who violated rules they applied five grades of punishment, and in examination and instruction they performed duties like the doctors.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifiers and registrars enforced school rules, imposing five grades of punishment on violators and sharing the doctors' examination and instructional duties.

sentences.zh: 職事學錄五人，掌與正、錄通掌學規。

translations.literal: Five duty registrars, together with the rectifiers and registrars, jointly enforced school regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Five duty registrars shared enforcement of school regulations with the rectifiers and registrars.

sentences.zh: 學諭二十人，掌以所授經傳諭諸生，直學四人，掌諸生之籍及幾察出入。

translations.literal: Twenty instructors expounded the classics and commentaries assigned to them; four direct learners managed student registers and supervised entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty instructors expounded the classics assigned to them; four direct learners maintained student registers and supervised comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 凡八十齊，齋置長、諭各一人，掌表率齋生，凡戾規矩者，糾以齊規五等之罰，仍月考齋生行藝，著於籍。

translations.literal: There were eighty dormitories; each dormitory had one head and one instructor who set an example for dormitory students, corrected violators with five grades of dormitory punishment, and still monthly examined dormitory students' conduct and learning, recording them in the register.
translations.idiomatic: There were eighty dormitories, each with a head and instructor who set an example, imposed five grades of dormitory punishment on rule-breakers, and monthly recorded students' conduct and learning.

sentences.zh: 武學博士、學諭各二人，掌以兵書、弓馬、武藝訓誘學者。

translations.literal: Two Military College doctors and two instructors each instructed learners in military books, archery and horsemanship, and martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Two Military College doctors and two instructors taught military texts, archery, horsemanship, and martial arts.

sentences.zh: 律學博士二人，掌傳授法律及校試之事。

translations.literal: Two Law College doctors transmitted law and handled examination matters.
translations.idiomatic: Two Law College doctors taught law and administered examinations.

sentences.zh: 小學，置職事教諭二人，掌訓導及考校責罰。

translations.literal: At the Primary School, two duty instructors were established to manage instruction and examination and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Primary School had two duty instructors who supervised instruction, examinations, and discipline.

sentences.zh: 學長二人，掌充齒位、糾不如儀者。

translations.literal: Two student prefects managed seating order and corrected those not observing ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Two student prefects managed seating order and corrected breaches of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 集正二人，掌籍諸生名氏，糾程課不逮者。

translations.literal: Two record rectifiers registered students' names and corrected those falling short in coursework.
translations.idiomatic: Two record rectifiers maintained student rolls and flagged those falling behind in coursework.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，詔用經術取士，廣闊黌舍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, an edict ordered selection of officials by classical learning and broad expansion of academy buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining an edict mandated selection of officials by classical learning and a major expansion of academy facilities.

sentences.zh: 分為三學，增置生徒，總二千八百人。

translations.literal: They were divided into three schools, student enrollment was increased, and the total reached 2,800.
translations.idiomatic: The academy was divided into three schools, enrollment was expanded, and the total reached 2,800 students.

sentences.zh: 隸籍有數，給食有等，庫書有官，治疾有醫。

translations.literal: Registry rolls had fixed numbers, rations had grades, the book storehouse had officials, and treating illness had physicians.
translations.idiomatic: Enrollment rolls were fixed, rations were graded by rank, the library had its own officials, and medical care was provided.

sentences.zh: 分案八，置吏十。

translations.literal: Eight desks were divided and ten clerks were established.
translations.idiomatic: Eight administrative desks were set up and ten clerks were appointed.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，詔自今奏舉太學博士，先以所業進呈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered that from then on, when memorializing to recommend Imperial College doctors, their written work should first be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1080 an edict required that nominees for Imperial College doctor first submit their scholarly work for review.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔國子監官差承務郎以上，闕即差選人充正官，立行、守、試請奉法。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered that Imperial Academy officials be assigned at the rank of Gentleman for Court Service or above; when posts were vacant, selectees were assigned as regular officials, and rules were established for provisional, acting, and trial appointment salaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 an edict required Imperial Academy officials to hold the rank of Gentleman for Court Service or higher; vacancies were filled by selectees as regular appointees, and salary rules were set for provisional, acting, and trial posts.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔罷太學保任同罪法。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict abolished the Imperial College mutual-guarantee shared-punishment law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1085 an edict abolished the Imperial College rule holding guarantors liable for the same offense as those they recommended.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，詔太學每歲公試，以司業、博士主之，如春秋補試法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered that the Imperial College's annual public examination be presided over by the Vice-Director and doctors, following the spring and autumn supplementary examination method.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086 an edict mandated annual public examinations at the Imperial College, presided over by the Vice-Director and doctors under the same rules as the spring and autumn supplementary exams.

sentences.zh: 左司諫王嚴叟言：「太學生補中人，乞並許應舉，罷一年之限。」

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Bureau remonstrator Wang Yansou said: "Imperial College students who pass the supplementary examination should all be permitted to take the civil service examinations, abolishing the one-year waiting period."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou of the Left Remonstrance Bureau said: "Imperial College students who pass the supplementary exam should be allowed to sit for the civil service examinations immediately, without the one-year waiting period."

sentences.zh: 詔國子監立法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Imperial Academy to draft regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Imperial Academy to draft regulations.

sentences.zh: 又詔給事中孫覺、秘書少監顧臨、崇政殿說書程頤、國子監長貳看詳修立國子監條例。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Supervising Secretary Sun Jue, Vice Director of the Secretariat Gu Lin, Chongzheng Hall Lecturer Cheng Yi, and the chief and vice directors of the Imperial Academy to review and draft Imperial Academy regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Supervising Secretary Sun Jue, Vice Director of the Secretariat Gu Lin, Chongzheng Hall Lecturer Cheng Yi, and the Imperial Academy's chief and vice directors to review and draft new academy regulations.

sentences.zh: 又詔置《春秋》博士一員，二年，增司業一員。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered establishment of one doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》; in the second year, one Vice-Director was added.
translations.idiomatic: The court also established one doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》; in 1089 one additional Vice-Director was added.

sentences.zh: 又詔內外學官選年三十以上曆任人充。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered that inner and outer school officials be chosen from those thirty years of age or older who had served in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court also required that school officials inside and outside the capital be drawn from incumbent officials aged thirty or above.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔國子監置長貳。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered establishment of chief and vice directors at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088 an edict restored chief and vice director posts at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔太學正、錄依熙寧法，選上舍生充，闕則以內舍生。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that Imperial College rectifiers and registrars follow the Xining method, chosen from upper-dormitory students, and when posts were vacant, from inner-dormitory students.
translations.idiomatic: In 1089 an edict restored the Xining practice of appointing Imperial College rectifiers and registrars from upper-dormitory students, with inner-dormitory students filling vacancies.

sentences.zh: 五年，殿中侍御史岑象求言：「國子監無叩問師資之益，學官不以訓導為己任，補試伺察不嚴，有假手之弊。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Palace Attendant Censor Cen Xiangqiu said: "The Imperial Academy offers no benefit for students seeking instruction from teachers; school officials do not take instruction as their duty; supplementary examinations are not strictly supervised, and there is the abuse of ghostwriting."
translations.idiomatic: In 1090 Palace Attendant Censor Cen Xiangqiu said: "Students at the Imperial Academy gain little from consulting their teachers; school officials neglect instruction; supplementary exams are poorly supervised; and ghostwriting is rampant."

sentences.zh: 詔禮部相度以聞，本部言：「生員遇有請益，許見長貳。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to assess the matter and report; that ministry said: "When students wish to ask for instruction, they should be permitted to see the chief and vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to study the matter and report back; it proposed that students seeking instruction be allowed to consult the chief and vice directors.

sentences.zh: 仍詔生員以所納齊課於講堂上指諭，並委博士逐月巡所隸齋，詢考生員所業。

translations.literal: It was further ordered that students present their submitted coursework for instruction in the lecture hall, and that doctors be charged monthly to inspect the dormitories under their jurisdiction and examine students' work.
translations.idiomatic: The court also required students to present submitted coursework for review in the lecture hall and assigned doctors to inspect their dormitories monthly and examine students' progress.

sentences.zh: 凡私試不鎖宿，欲令不罷講說。」

translations.literal: All private examinations would not require overnight confinement, intending that lecturing not be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: Private examinations would no longer require overnight confinement, so that regular instruction would not be interrupted."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，監察御史劉拯言：「太學復行元豐中三舍推恩注官、免省試、免解試之制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, Investigating Censor Liu Zheng said: "The Imperial College has restored the Yuanfeng system of the three dormitories granting favor, appointment to office, exemption from the provincial examination, and exemption from the qualifying examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1094 Investigating Censor Liu Zheng said: "The Imperial College has restored the Yuanfeng three-dormitory system of preferment, direct appointment, and exemption from provincial and qualifying examinations.

sentences.zh: 夫舊法欲行，必先嚴考察。

translations.literal: If an old law is to be implemented, strict evaluation must come first.
translations.idiomatic: For an old system to work, evaluation must first be rigorously enforced.

sentences.zh: 請自今太學長貳、博士、正錄，選學行純備、從所推服者為之，有弛慢不公，考察不實，則重加譴責。

translations.literal: He requested that from now on the chief and vice directors, doctors, rectifiers, and registrars of the Imperial College be chosen from those of pure learning and conduct whom students respect; if any were negligent, unfair, or evaluated falsely, they should be heavily censured.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Imperial College chiefs, vice directors, doctors, rectifiers, and registrars hereafter be chosen for pure learning and conduct that students respect, with heavy penalties for negligence, bias, or false evaluation.

sentences.zh: 差職掌長諭改正如元豐舊制。」

translations.literal: Assignment of duty-holders, dormitory heads, and instructors should be corrected to follow the old Yuanfeng system."
translations.idiomatic: The assignment of duty officers, dormitory heads, and instructors should be restored to the Yuanfeng system."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「內外學官非製科、進士出身及上舍生入官者，並罷。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "School officials inside and outside the capital who were not graduates of the special decree examinations or the jinshi examination, nor upper-dormitory students who entered office, were all dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict dismissed all school officials inside and outside the capital who were not special-decree or jinshi graduates and had not entered office through the upper dormitory."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「太學正、錄依元豐舊制，各置五人。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Imperial College rectifiers and registrars, following the old Yuanfeng system, were each established at five posts."
translations.idiomatic: The court also restored the Yuanfeng quota of five rectifiers and five registrars at the Imperial College."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「太學三舍生並依元豐學製，重行考察，依舊條推恩。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Imperial College students of the three dormitories all followed the Yuanfeng school system, with evaluation re-enforced and favor granted according to the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Imperial College students in all three dormitories to follow the Yuanfeng system, with rigorous evaluation and preferment under the old rules."

sentences.zh: 左司諫翟思言：「元豐《太學令》訓迪糾禁亦具矣，今追復經義取士，乞令有司看詳，依舊頒行。」

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Bureau remonstrator Zhai Si said: "The Yuanfeng 《Imperial College Statutes》 already fully set forth instruction and disciplinary prohibitions; now that the New Text classics are restored for selecting officials, I beg that the responsible offices review them and reissue them according to the old practice."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Si of the Left Remonstrance Bureau said: "The Yuanfeng 《Imperial College Statutes》 already provide full rules for instruction and discipline; now that New Text classicism has been restored for recruitment, he asked the responsible offices to review and reissue them."

sentences.zh: 詔送國子監，又詔：「內外學官選進士出身及經明行修人。」

translations.literal: An edict sent the matter to the Imperial Academy; another edict stated: "School officials inside and outside the capital were chosen from jinshi graduates and men of classics mastery and virtuous conduct."
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Imperial Academy; the court also ordered that school officials be chosen from jinshi graduates and men recommended for classics mastery and virtuous conduct."

sentences.zh: 又詔學官並召試，國子監長貳、台諫官、外監司皆許薦舉。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered that all school officials be summoned for examination; the chief and vice directors of the Imperial Academy, remonstrance and censorial officials, and outer supervisory commissioners were all permitted to recommend candidates.
translations.idiomatic: School officials were also required to pass a summons examination; the Imperial Academy's chief and vice directors, censorial officials, and external supervisory commissioners were all authorized to recommend candidates.

sentences.zh: 三年，司業龔原言：「公試依元豐舊制，以長貳監試，輪差博士五員考試，乞朝廷更差官五員參考。」

translations.literal: In the third year, Vice-Director Gong Yuan said: "Public examinations follow the old Yuanfeng system, with the chief and vice directors supervising the exam and five doctors assigned in rotation to examine; I beg that the court assign five additional officials to assist in grading."
translations.idiomatic: In 1096 Vice-Director Gong Yuan said: "Public exams follow the Yuanfeng system, with the chief and vice directors supervising and five doctors assigned in rotation to grade them; he asked the court to appoint five additional officials to assist."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，詔有官人許入太學充監生，毋過四十人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, an edict permitted incumbent officials to enter the Imperial College as directorate students, not exceeding forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1098 an edict allowed incumbent officials to enroll at the Imperial College as directorate students, up to a maximum of forty.

sentences.zh: 三年，復置《春秋》博士。

translations.literal: In the third year, the doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1100 the doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 was restored.

sentences.zh: 〈（崇寧元年省罷。）〉

translations.literal: (Abolished by reduction in the first year of Chongning.)
translations.idiomatic: (Abolished in 1102.)

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，宰臣蔡京言：「有詔天下皆興學貢士，以三舍考選法遍行天下，聽每三年貢入太學。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, Chief Councillor Cai Jing said: "There is an edict that throughout the realm schools should be established and tribute scholars presented; the three-dormitory examination-and-selection method should be applied everywhere, permitting tribute entry to the Imperial College every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In 1102 Chief Councillor Cai Jing said: "An edict has ordered schools established empire-wide and tribute scholars sent up; the three-dormitory examination system should be applied everywhere, with tribute scholars admitted to the Imperial College every three years.

sentences.zh: 上合試仍別為考，分為三等，若試中上等，補充太學上舍，試中中等、下等者，補充內舍，餘為外舍生，仍建外學於國之南，待其歲考行藝，升之太學。

translations.literal: The upper-dormitory examination would still be separately examined and divided into three grades; if one tested into the upper grade, one was supplemented into the Imperial College upper dormitory; if one tested into the middle or lower grade, one was supplemented into the inner dormitory; the rest became outer-dormitory students; an Outer Academy was still built south of the capital, awaiting their annual evaluation of conduct and learning before promotion to the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-dormitory candidates would be separately examined and ranked in three grades: the top grade entered the Imperial College upper dormitory, the middle and lower grades entered the inner dormitory, and the remainder became outer-dormitory students; an Outer Academy was established south of the capital, where students would be promoted to the Imperial College after annual evaluation of conduct and learning.

sentences.zh: 其外學官屬：司業一人，丞一人，博士十人，學正五人，學錄五人；

translations.literal: Its Outer Academy staff were: one Vice-Director, one assistant, ten doctors, five rectifiers, and five registrars;
translations.idiomatic: The Outer Academy staff comprised one Vice-Director, one assistant, ten doctors, five rectifiers, and five registrars;

sentences.zh: 職事人係學生充；

translations.literal: duty officers were filled by students;
translations.idiomatic: duty officers were drawn from the student body;

sentences.zh: 學錄五人，學諭十人，直學二人，齋長、齋諭各一人。

translations.literal: five registrars, ten instructors, two direct scholars, and one dormitory head and one dormitory instructor each.
translations.idiomatic: five registrars, ten instructors, two direct scholars, and one dormitory head and one dormitory instructor for each dormitory.

sentences.zh: 外舍生三千人，太學上舍一百人，內舍三百人，候將來貢試到合格者，即上合以二百人、內舍以六百人為額。

translations.literal: Outer-dormitory students numbered 3,000; Imperial College upper dormitory 100; inner dormitory 300; when tribute examinees in the future reached qualified numbers, the upper dormitory quota would become 200 and the inner dormitory 600.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-dormitory enrollment was set at 3,000, the Imperial College upper dormitory at 100, and the inner dormitory at 300; once enough qualified tribute examinees were available, the upper dormitory quota would rise to 200 and the inner dormitory to 600.

sentences.zh: 處上舍、內舍於太學，處外舍於外學。

translations.literal: The upper and inner dormitories were placed in the Imperial College; the outer dormitory was placed in the Outer Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The upper and inner dormitories were housed in the Imperial College; the outer dormitory was housed in the Outer Academy.

sentences.zh: 外學置齋一百，講堂四，每齋三十人。

translations.literal: The Outer Academy established one hundred dormitories and four lecture halls, thirty persons per dormitory.
translations.idiomatic: The Outer Academy had one hundred dormitories and four lecture halls, with thirty students per dormitory.

sentences.zh: 太學自訟齋移於外學。

translations.literal: The Imperial College Hall of Self-Reproach was moved to the Outer Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial College's Hall of Self-Reproach was transferred to the Outer Academy.

sentences.zh: 諸路貢士並入外學，候依法考選校試合格，升之太學為上舍、內舍生。

translations.literal: Tribute scholars from all circuits all entered the Outer Academy; awaiting lawful examination, selection, and verification as qualified, they were promoted to the Imperial College as upper- and inner-dormitory students.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute scholars from all circuits entered the Outer Academy first and, once they passed the prescribed examinations and evaluations, were promoted to the Imperial College as upper- or inner-dormitory students.

sentences.zh: 見為太學外舍生，依舊在太學，候外學成日取旨。

translations.literal: Those currently Imperial College outer-dormitory students remained in the Imperial College as before, awaiting imperial decision when the Outer Academy was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Current Imperial College outer-dormitory students remained where they were until the Outer Academy was completed and the court issued further orders.

sentences.zh: 外學並依太學敕、令、格、式。」

translations.literal: The Outer Academy altogether followed Imperial College edicts, statutes, precedents, and regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The Outer Academy was governed by the same edicts, statutes, precedents, and regulations as the Imperial College."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年，罷《春秋》博士。

translations.literal: In the second year, the doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1103 the doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 was abolished.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔辟雍置司成、司業各一員。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered that Piyong establish one Director of Studies and one Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1104 an edict established one Director of Studies and one Vice-Director at Piyong.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：「辟雍待四方貢士，在國之郊，太學教養上舍生，在王城之內，內上既殊，高下未倫；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict stated: "Piyong receives tribute scholars from the four directions and lies in the capital's suburbs; the Imperial College nurtures upper-dormitory students within the royal city; inner and upper are already distinct, yet high and low are not properly ordered;
translations.idiomatic: In 1105 an edict noted: "Piyong, in the capital suburbs, receives tribute scholars from all directions, while the Imperial College within the royal city nurtures upper-dormitory students; though inner and upper ranks are distinct, their relative standing is not properly ordered;

sentences.zh: 辟雍有司成在侍郎之次，國子有祭酒、司業列於卿、少，事體不順，合行厘正。」

translations.literal: Piyong's Director of Studies ranks after Vice Ministers, while the Imperial Academy's Director and Vice-Director are arrayed among Grandees and Vice Grandees; the institutional arrangement is improper and should be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: Piyong's Director of Studies ranked below Vice Ministers, while the Imperial Academy's Director and Vice-Director stood among Grandees and Vice Grandees—an improper arrangement that required correction."

sentences.zh: 改辟雍司成為太學司成，總國子監及內外學事，凡學之事，皆許專達。

translations.literal: Piyong's Director of Studies was changed to Imperial College Director of Studies, overseeing the Imperial Academy and inner and outer academy affairs; all academy matters were permitted direct memorialization.
translations.idiomatic: Piyong's Director of Studies was renamed Imperial College Director of Studies, with authority over the Imperial Academy and all inner and outer schools; he was empowered to memorialize directly on all academic affairs.

sentences.zh: 仍立學官謁禁。

translations.literal: Rules prohibiting school officials from receiving visitors were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Rules were also established forbidding school officials from receiving private visits.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，置國子博士四員，國子正、錄各二員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, four Imperial Academy doctors were established, and two rectifiers and two registrars each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107 four Imperial Academy doctors were established, along with two rectifiers and two registrars.

sentences.zh: 太學、辟雍博士共置二十員，國子、太學每經一員，辟雍二員。

translations.literal: Imperial College and Piyong doctors together totaled twenty posts: one for each classic at the Imperial Academy and Imperial College, and two at Piyong.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty doctors were established for the Imperial College and Piyong combined: one per classic at the Imperial Academy and Imperial College, and two at Piyong.

sentences.zh: 從薛昂之請也。

translations.literal: This followed Xue Ang's request.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a memorial from Xue Ang.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔諸路贍學餘錢並起發充在京學事支用。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered that surplus school-support funds from all circuits be forwarded to cover capital academy expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1109 an edict ordered surplus school-support funds from all circuits forwarded to cover educational expenses in the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔省國子、辟雍博士五員，太學命官學錄一員，辟雍二員，國子命官正、錄及命官直學、國子監書庫官等官，並省罷，依紹聖格，毋用謄錄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict reduced Imperial Academy and Piyong doctors by five posts, Imperial College appointed registrars by one post and Piyong by two posts, and Imperial Academy appointed rectifiers and registrars, appointed direct scholars, Imperial Academy library officials, and similar posts were all abolished by reduction; following Shaosheng precedents, copying clerks were not used.
translations.idiomatic: In 1110 five Imperial Academy and Piyong doctor posts were cut, along with one appointed Imperial College registrar and two at Piyong; appointed rectifiers, registrars, direct scholars, and Imperial Academy library officials were all abolished; under Shaosheng precedents, copying clerks were no longer employed.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，詔兩學博士、正、錄依舊制選試，朝廷除授。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered that doctors, rectifiers, and registrars of both academies be selected by examination under the old system and appointed by the court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1111 an edict restored the old practice of selecting doctors, rectifiers, and registrars at both academies by examination and appointing them by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 七年，新提舉河東路學事王格言：「崇寧初，建辟雍於郊，以處貢士及外舍生，立太學於國，以處上舍、內舍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the newly appointed Supervisor of Hedong Circuit School Affairs Wang Ge said: "At the beginning of Chongning, Piyong was built in the suburbs to house tribute scholars and outer-dormitory students, and the Imperial College was established in the capital to house the upper and inner dormitories.
translations.idiomatic: In 1117 Wang Ge, newly appointed to supervise school affairs in Hedong Circuit, said: "When Chongning reforms began, Piyong was built in the suburbs for tribute scholars and outer-dormitory students, and the Imperial College in the capital for the upper and inner dormitories.

sentences.zh: 由州、郡而貢之辟雍，由辟雍而升之太學。

translations.literal: From prefectures and commanderies they were tribute-presented to Piyong, and from Piyong they were promoted to the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars were sent up from prefectures and commanderies to Piyong, and from Piyong promoted to the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 法行之初，上、內舍之選未眾，故外舍有校定者留太學，無校定者出辟雍。

translations.literal: When the law was first implemented, selections for the upper and inner dormitories were not yet numerous, so outer-dormitory students with finalized evaluations remained in the Imperial College, and those without went to Piyong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the system's operation, upper- and inner-dormitory places were still scarce, so evaluated outer-dormitory students remained in the Imperial College while unevaluated ones went to Piyong.

sentences.zh: 比年上、內舍人日增，而太學又有國子隨行親及小學生，人數已多，居處迫隘，乞以外舍生有無校定，並居辟雍，升補上、內舍乃入太學。」

translations.literal: In recent years upper- and inner-dormitory numbers have daily increased, while the Imperial College also has directorate attendants and primary school students; the population is already large and living quarters cramped; I beg that outer-dormitory students, whether or not they have finalized evaluations, all reside at Piyong, entering the Imperial College only upon promotion to the upper or inner dormitories."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years upper- and inner-dormitory enrollment had grown, and the Imperial College also housed directorate attendants and primary school students; quarters were overcrowded; he asked that all outer-dormitory students, evaluated or not, reside at Piyong and enter the Imperial College only upon promotion to the upper or inner dormitories."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔兩博士、正、錄並諸州教授兼用元豐試法，仍止試一經。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered that doctors, rectifiers, and registrars at both academies and prefectural instructors all concurrently use the Yuanfeng examination method, still testing only one classic.
translations.idiomatic: In 1118 an edict required doctors, rectifiers, and registrars at both academies and prefectural instructors to be selected under the Yuanfeng examination system, testing only one classic.

sentences.zh: 吏部具到元豐法：進士第一甲，或省試十名內，或府、監發解五名內，或太學公、私試三名內，或季試兩次為第一人，或上舍、內舍生，或曾充經論以上職掌，或投所業乞試，並聽試，入上等注博士，中下等注正、錄，即人多闕少，原注諸州教授者聽。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel submitted the Yuanfeng law: first-rank jinshi, or within the top ten of the provincial examination, or within the top five of prefecture and directorate qualifying examinations, or within the top three of Imperial College public or private examinations, or first place twice in quarterly examinations, or upper- and inner-dormitory students, or those who had served as classic-discourse duty officers or above, or those submitting their work to request examination—all were permitted to test; those entering the upper grade were assigned as doctors, those in the middle and lower grades as rectifiers and registrars; where many qualified but posts were few, those originally assigned as prefectural instructors were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel submitted the Yuanfeng rules: first-rank jinshi, top ten provincial graduates, top five prefectural qualifiers, top three on Imperial College public or private exams, twice-first in quarterly exams, upper- and inner-dormitory students, former classic-discourse duty officers, and those submitting work for examination were all eligible; upper-grade passers were appointed doctors, middle- and lower-grade passers rectifiers and registrars; where candidates outnumbered posts, appointees originally slated for prefectural instructor posts were also accepted.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，詔罷天下三舍，太學以三舍考選，開封府及諸路以科舉取士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe, an edict abolished the three dormitories throughout the realm; the Imperial College selected by the three-dormitory examination method, while Kaifeng Prefecture and all circuits selected officials by the civil examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1121 an edict abolished the three-dormitory system empire-wide; the Imperial College alone retained three-dormitory selection, while Kaifeng and the circuits returned to civil examination recruitment.

sentences.zh: 州學未行三舍以前，應置學宮及養士去處，依元豐舊制。

translations.literal: For prefectural schools before the three dormitories were implemented, sites for school buildings and student support should follow the old Yuanfeng system.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural schools that had not yet adopted the three-dormitory system were to follow Yuanfeng arrangements for school buildings and student support.

sentences.zh: 太學生並撥填舊額，辟雍正額入太學者，撥入額外，依舊制遇填闕。

translations.literal: Imperial College students were all reassigned to fill old quotas; those from Piyong's regular quota entering the Imperial College were assigned to extra quota, filling vacancies according to the old system when they arose.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College students were reassigned to existing quotas; Piyong regular-quota students entering the Imperial College were placed on supplemental rolls and filled vacancies under the old rules.

sentences.zh: 諸內舍上等校定人願入太學者，與免補試。

translations.literal: Inner-dormitory students with upper-grade finalized evaluations who wished to enter the Imperial College were granted exemption from the supplementary examination.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-dormitory students with upper-grade evaluations who wished to enter the Imperial College were exempted from the supplementary exam.

sentences.zh: 辟雍官屬並罷。

translations.literal: Piyong staff were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All Piyong staff posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 又詔國子博士、正、錄改充太學正、錄。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Imperial Academy doctors, rectifiers, and registrars changed to serve as Imperial College rectifiers and registrars.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Imperial Academy doctors, rectifiers, and registrars reassigned as Imperial College rectifiers and registrars.

sentences.zh: 七年，臣僚言：「熙、豐間，博士未嘗除代，近年以來，席未暖而代者已至當從正、錄第進。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, officials said: "During the Xi and Feng period, doctors were never replaced in succession; in recent years, before their seats had warmed replacements had arrived; they should advance from rectifier and registrar ranks in order.
translations.idiomatic: In 1125 officials noted: "Under the Xi and Feng reforms, doctors were not rapidly replaced; recently successors arrived before incumbents had settled in; doctors should advance through rectifier and registrar ranks in order.

sentences.zh: 新除太學博士胡世將、周利建乞改除正、錄，候將來升為博士。」

translations.literal: The newly appointed Imperial College doctors Hu Shijiang and Zhou Lijian requested reassignment as rectifiers and registrars, awaiting future promotion to doctor."
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed Imperial College doctors Hu Shijiang and Zhou Lijian asked to be reassigned as rectifiers and registrars pending future promotion to doctor."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，諫議大夫馮澥言：「朝廷罷元祐學術之禁，不專王氏之學，《六經》之旨，其說是者取之，今學校或主一偏之說，執一偏之見，願詔有司考校，敢私好惡去取，重行黜責。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, Remonstrance and Policy Grandee Feng Xi said: "The court has abolished the Yuanyou ban on scholarly schools, no longer exclusively following Master Wang's learning; the purport of the 《Six Classics》—whichever interpretation is correct should be adopted; now schools sometimes uphold one partial doctrine and cling to one partial view; I wish an edict ordering responsible offices to examine and verify; those who dare privately apply likes and dislikes in selection should be heavily dismissed and punished."
translations.idiomatic: In 1126 Remonstrance and Policy Grandee Feng Xi said: "The court has lifted the Yuanyou ban on rival scholarly schools and no longer enforces Wang Anshi's learning alone; whichever interpretation of the 《Six Classics》 is sound should be accepted; yet some schools still cling to partisan doctrines; he asked that responsible offices investigate, and that officials who let private bias govern teaching be severely punished."

sentences.zh: 又詔太學博士替成資闕。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered that Imperial College doctor replacements become regular seniority vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ruled that vacated Imperial College doctor posts would count as regular seniority vacancies.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，詔國子監並歸禮部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, an edict ordered the Imperial Academy transferred altogether to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1129 an edict placed the Imperial Academy under the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔復養生徒，置博士。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered restoration of student support and establishment of doctors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict restored student enrollment and reestablished doctor posts.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年，置祭酒、司業各一人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing, one Director and one Vice-Director were established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1142 one Director and one Vice-Director were appointed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，太學成，增置博士、正、錄。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Imperial College was completed, doctors, rectifiers, and registrars were added.
translations.idiomatic: In 1143, when the Imperial College was completed, additional doctors, rectifiers, and registrars were appointed.

sentences.zh: 參用元祐、紹聖監學法，修立監學新法。

translations.literal: Drawing on Yuanyou and Shaosheng directorate school laws, new directorate school regulations were drafted.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on Yuanyou and Shaosheng academy regulations, new directorate school rules were drafted.

sentences.zh: 詔國子博士、正、錄通治諸齋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Imperial Academy doctors, rectifiers, and registrars to oversee all dormitories jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required Imperial Academy doctors, rectifiers, and registrars to oversee all dormitories jointly.

sentences.zh: 學官闕，從本監選舉。

translations.literal: When school official posts were vacant, selection was made from within the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Vacant school official posts were filled by selection within the directorate.

sentences.zh: 其後，監學博士、正、錄增減不齊，兼攝並置不一。

translations.literal: Thereafter, directorate school doctors, rectifiers, and registrars increased and decreased unevenly, and concurrent acting appointments were not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the numbers of directorate doctors, rectifiers, and registrars fluctuated, and concurrent acting appointments varied.

sentences.zh: 至隆興以後，正、錄不兼權，祭酒、司業並置，復書庫官；

translations.literal: From Longxing onward, rectifiers and registrars no longer concurrently held acting posts; Director and Vice-Director were both established, and library officials were restored;
translations.idiomatic: From the Longxing era onward, rectifiers and registrars no longer held concurrent acting posts; both Director and Vice-Director were maintained, and library officials were restored;

sentences.zh: 又定國子博士一員，太學博士三員，正、錄共四員，學官之制始定。

translations.literal: One Imperial Academy doctor, three Imperial College doctors, and four rectifiers and registrars together were fixed, and the school official system was first settled.
translations.idiomatic: The establishment was fixed at one Imperial Academy doctor, three Imperial College doctors, and four rectifiers and registrars combined—the school official system was finally settled.

sentences.zh: 淳熙四年，置監門官一員，兼管石經閣，以不厘務使臣充，以後相承不改。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunxi, one gate-keeper official was established, concurrently managing the Stone Classics Pavilion, filled by an unattached commissioner; this continued unchanged thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1177 one gate-keeper official was appointed, also overseeing the Stone Classics Pavilion, filled by an unattached commissioner—a practice thereafter unchanged.

sentences.zh: 【武學】慶曆三年，詔置武學於武成王廟，以阮逸為教授。

translations.literal: 【Military College】 In the third year of Qingli, an edict established the Military College at the Temple of King Wucheng, with Ruan Yi as instructor.
translations.idiomatic: 【Military College】 In 1043 an edict established the Military College at the Temple of King Wucheng, appointing Ruan Yi as instructor.

sentences.zh: 八月，罷武學，以議者言「古名將如諸葛亮、羊祜、杜預等，豈專學係、吳」故也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Military College was abolished, because critics said "ancient famous generals such as Zhuge Liang, Yang Hu, and Du Yu—how could they have studied only Sun and Wu?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Military College was abolished after critics argued that great generals such as Zhuge Liang, Yang Hu, and Du Yu had not mastered only Sun Wu and Wu Qi.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，樞密院言：「古者出師受成於學，文武弛張，其道一也，乞復置武學。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "In antiquity armies on campaign received consecration at the academy; civil and military expand and contract, yet their Way is one; I beg restoration of the Military College."
translations.idiomatic: In 1072 the Bureau of Military Affairs argued: "In antiquity armies received consecration at the academy before marching; civil and military arts were two expressions of one Way; it asked that the Military College be restored."

sentences.zh: 詔於武成王廟置學。

translations.literal: An edict established the school at the Temple of King Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reestablished the school at the Temple of King Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，改教授為博士，紹興十六年，詔修建武學，武博、武諭以兵書、弓馬、武藝誘誨學者。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng bureaucratic system was implemented, instructor was changed to doctor; in the sixteenth year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered reconstruction of the Military College; military doctors and military instructors used military books, archery and horsemanship, and martial arts to guide and instruct learners.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuanfeng reforms the instructor title became doctor; in 1146 an edict ordered the Military College rebuilt; military doctors and instructors taught military texts, archery, horsemanship, and martial arts.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十六年，詔武學博士、學諭各置一員，內博士於文臣有出身或武舉出身曾預高選棄，其學諭差武學人，後又除文臣之有出身者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing, an edict established one military doctor and one instructor each; for the doctor post, civil officials with examination credentials or military examination graduates who had ranked in the high selection were considered; military instructors were assigned from Military College personnel, and later civil officials with credentials were also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1156 one military doctor and one instructor were established; the doctor was drawn from credentialed civil officials or military examination graduates who had ranked highly; instructors were first assigned from Military College personnel, and later credentialed civil officials were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 【宗學】元豐六年，宗室令鑠乞建宗學，詔從之，既而中輟，建中靖國元年復置。

translations.literal: 【Clan Academy】 In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, imperial clansman Commandant Ling requested establishment of a Clan Academy; an edict approved it, but it was soon suspended, and in the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: 【Clan Academy】 In 1083 imperial clansman Commandant Ling petitioned to establish a Clan Academy; the court approved, but the project was soon halted and restored in 1101.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，立月書、季考法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, monthly record and quarterly examination methods were established.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning era monthly progress records and quarterly examinations were instituted.

sentences.zh: 南渡初，建學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the southward crossing, the academy was built.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled south, the academy was reestablished.

sentences.zh: 嘉定更新置四齋，後再增三齋。

translations.literal: In the Jiading renewal, four dormitories were newly established; later three more dormitories were added.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading restoration four dormitories were added, and three more were added later.

sentences.zh: 宗學博士，舊諸王宮大、小學教授也。

translations.literal: Clan Academy doctors were formerly the great and small school instructors of the princely palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The Clan Academy doctor had formerly been the instructor of the great and small schools in the princely palaces.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，太宗將為皇侄等置師傅，執政謂環衛之官非新王比，當有降，乃以教授為名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, Emperor Taizong was about to appoint tutors for the imperial nephews and others; the chief ministers said that Imperial Guard officials were not comparable to newly enfeoffed princes and ought to receive a reduction in rank, so the title instructor was used.
translations.idiomatic: In 995, when Emperor Taizong prepared to appoint tutors for his imperial nephews, the chief ministers argued that Imperial Guard officers could not be ranked on a par with newly enfeoffed princes and deserved a lower appointment; the post was therefore styled instructor.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遂命諸王府官分兼南、北宅教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, princely palace officials were then ordered to serve concurrently as instructors of the Southern and Northern Residences.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping era princely palace officials were ordered to serve concurrently as instructors of the Southern and Northern Residences.

sentences.zh: 南宮者，太祖、太宗諸王之子孫處之，所謂睦親宅也。

translations.literal: The Southern Palace was where the sons and grandsons of the princes of Taizu and Taizong were housed—the so-called Kindred-kin Residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Palace housed the sons and grandsons of the princes of Taizu and Taizong; it was what was called the Kindred-kin Residence.

sentences.zh: 崇寧五年，又改稱某王宮宗子博士，位國子博士之上。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning, the title was again changed to clan-son doctor of such-and-such princely palace, ranking above Imperial Academy doctors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1106 the post was renamed clan-son doctor of the princely palace in question, ranking above Imperial Academy doctors.

sentences.zh: 靖康之亂，宗學遂廢。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Jingkang, the Clan Academy was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Clan Academy was abolished in the upheaval of Jingkang.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，始復置諸王宮大小學教授二員，隆興省其一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, two instructors of the great and small schools of the princely palaces were first restored; in Longxing one was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134 two instructors for the great and small schools of the princely palaces were restored; in 1163 one post was cut.

sentences.zh: 喜定九年十二月，始復置宗學，改教授為博士，又置宗學諭一員，並隸宗正寺，在太常博士之下，諭在國子正之上，奉給、賞典依國子博士及正例，於是宗室疏遠者皆得就學。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year of Xiding, the Clan Academy was first restored; instructors were changed to doctors, and one Clan Academy instructor was also established; all were subordinate to the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs, ranking below Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctors, with the instructor above Imperial Academy rectifiers; salaries and reward precedents followed those for Imperial Academy doctors and rectifiers; thus distant members of the imperial clan were all able to attend school.
translations.idiomatic: In December 1216 the Clan Academy was restored; instructors became doctors, and a Clan Academy instructor was added. All posts were placed under the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs, below Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctors but with the instructor above Imperial Academy rectifiers. Salaries and honors followed Imperial Academy doctor and rectifier precedents, and distant clansmen were at last able to enroll.

sentences.zh: 旋有旨復存諸王宮大小學教授一員。

translations.literal: Soon an edict restored one instructor of the great and small schools of the princely palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict restored one instructor for the great and small schools of the princely palaces.

sentences.zh: 【書庫官】淳化五年，判國子監李誌言：「國子監舊有印書錢物所，名為近俗，乞改為國子監書庫官。」

translations.literal: 【Library Official】 In the fifth year of Chunhua, Imperial Academy chief commissioner Li Zhìyán said: "The Imperial Academy formerly had an office for printing books, funds, and goods; the name is rather vulgar; I request that it be changed to Imperial Academy library official."
translations.idiomatic: 【Library Official】 In 994 Imperial Academy chief commissioner Li Zhìyán said: "The Imperial Academy long maintained an office for book printing, funds, and supplies under a rather inelegant name; I ask that it be renamed the Imperial Academy library official."

sentences.zh: 始置書庫監官，以京朝官充。

translations.literal: Library supervisory officials were then first established, filled by capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: The court then established library supervisory officials, filled by capital officials.

sentences.zh: 掌印經史群書，以備朝廷宣索賜予之用，及出鬻而收其直以上於官。

translations.literal: They managed printing of the classics, histories, and other books, to supply the court's needs for summons, bestowal, and grant, and also sold copies and remitted the proceeds to the government.
translations.idiomatic: The office printed the classics, histories, and other books for court distribution and bestowal, and also sold copies and remitted the proceeds to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年省。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng it was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The post was abolished in 1080.

sentences.zh: 中興後，並國子監入禮部。

translations.literal: After the restoration, the Imperial Academy was transferred altogether to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the court's restoration south, the Imperial Academy was placed under the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年，復置一員；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, one post was restored;
translations.idiomatic: In 1143 one post was restored;

sentences.zh: 三十一年，罷。

translations.literal: in the thirty-first year, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: in 1161 it was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 隆興初，詔主簿兼書庫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longxing, an edict ordered the registrar to serve concurrently as library keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longxing era an edict assigned library duties to the registrar.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，復置一員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao, one post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1171 the post was restored.

sentences.zh: 【少府監】舊制，判監事一人。

translations.literal: 【Directorate for Imperial Manufacturers】 Under the old system, one chief commissioner of the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: 【Directorate for Imperial Manufacturers】 Under the old system there was one chief commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以朝官充。

translations.literal: Filled by a court official.
translations.idiomatic: The post was filled by a court official.

sentences.zh: 凡進禦器玩、后妃服飾、雕文錯彩工巧之事，分隸文思院、後苑造作所，本監但掌造門戟、神衣、旌節，郊廟諸壇祭玉、法物，鑄牌印諸記，百官拜表案、褥之事。

translations.literal: All matters of imperial playthings, empress and consort apparel, and carved and inlaid craftsmanship were separately assigned to the Literary Refinement Court and the Rear Garden Manufactories; this directorate only managed manufacture of gate halberds, spirit garments, banners and staffs, sacrificial jades and ritual objects for suburban and temple altars, casting of plaques, seals, and various inscriptions, and the petition desks and cushions used when officials bowed with memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial curios, empress and consort dress, and fine inlaid craftwork fell to the Literary Refinement Court and the Rear Garden Manufactories; the directorate itself made gate halberds, spirit vestments, banners and staffs, sacrificial jades and ritual objects for suburban and temple rites, cast plaques and seals, and the desks and cushions used when officials presented memorials.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，則供祭器、爵、瓚、照燭。

translations.literal: Whenever sacrifices were performed, it supplied sacrificial vessels, goblets, libation cups, and illumination candles.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices it supplied ritual vessels, goblets, libation cups, and candles.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，始置監、少監、丞、主簿各一人。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system was implemented, one director, vice-director, assistant, and registrar were first established.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng reforms took effect, the directorate was given one director, vice-director, assistant, and registrar.

sentences.zh: 監掌百工伎巧之政令，少監為之貳，丞參領之。

translations.literal: The director managed policies and orders for the hundred crafts and skilled arts; the vice-director was second to him, and the assistant shared in overseeing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The director oversaw policy for all skilled crafts; the vice-director assisted him, and the assistant shared administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 凡乘輿服御、寶冊、符印、旌節、度量權衡之制，與夫祭祀、朝會展采備物，皆率其屬以供焉。

translations.literal: All regulations for imperial carriage accoutrements, seals and registers, tallies and seals, banners and staffs, and weights and measures, as well as the display of regalia and prepared objects for sacrifices and court assemblies, were all led by its subordinates in supply.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinates supplied imperial carriage fittings, seals and registers, tallies and seals, banners and staffs, standards of measure, and all regalia and equipment for sacrifices and court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 庀其工徒，察其程課、作止勞逸及寒暑早晚之節，視將作匠法，物勒工名，以法式察其良窳。

translations.literal: It organized the artisans and laborers, inspected quotas, work and rest, labor and ease, and the seasons of cold and heat and early and late hours, followed the craftsmen's standards of the Directorate of Imperial Construction, inscribed artisans' names on objects, and examined quality and defect by the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: It organized artisans, monitored quotas and the balance of work and rest through the seasons, followed construction craftsmen's standards, required artisans' names to be marked on finished goods, and judged quality against the regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡金玉、犀象、羽毛、齒革、膠漆、材竹，辨其名物而考其制度，事當損益，則審其可否，議定以聞。

translations.literal: For gold and jade, rhinoceros horn and ivory, feathers, teeth and hides, lacquer and glue, timber and bamboo, it distinguished names and objects and examined their regulations; when matters required increase or reduction, it reviewed what was feasible, decided by deliberation, and reported.
translations.idiomatic: It catalogued gold, jade, rhinoceros horn, ivory, feathers, hides, lacquer, glue, timber, and bamboo, reviewed their specifications, and when changes were needed assessed feasibility, settled policy, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 少府所掌，舊有主名，其工作之事，則監自親之。

translations.literal: What the Directorate for Imperial Manufacturers controlled had established designations of responsibility; as for matters of actual work, the director personally oversaw them.
translations.idiomatic: Each function under the directorate had long had a designated name; in actual production the director personally supervised the work.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，已厘歸有司，官制行，皆復舊。

translations.literal: In the Xining period, affairs had already been reorganized and returned to the responsible offices; when the official system was implemented, all were restored to the old order.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reforms these functions had been reassigned to other offices; under the Yuanfeng system they were all restored.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，工部言：「文思院上下界諸作工料條格，該說不盡，功限例各寬剩，乞委官檢照前後料例功限，編為定式。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, the Ministry of Works said: "The regulations on materials for the various workshops of the upper and lower divisions of the Literary Refinement Court do not fully cover all cases, and the work quotas are in each instance overly generous; I request that officials be delegated to examine earlier and later material precedents and work quotas and compile them into fixed regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In 1078 the Ministry of Works reported: "Material rules for the upper and lower divisions of the Literary Refinement Court are incomplete, and work quotas are uniformly too generous; please appoint officials to review past and present material and quota precedents and codify them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「文思監官除內侍外，令工部、少府監同議選差。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Apart from inner attendants, Literary Refinement supervisory officials shall be jointly selected and assigned by the Ministry of Works and the Directorate for Imperial Manufacturers after consultation."
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered: "Except for inner attendants, Literary Refinement supervisors were to be chosen jointly by the Ministry of Works and the Directorate for Imperial Manufacturers."

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，詔：「文思院兩界監官，立定文臣一員、武臣二員。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, an edict stated: "For the supervisory officials of both divisions of the Literary Refinement Court, one civil official and two military officials were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1104 an edict ordered: "For the Literary Refinement Court's two divisions, one civil and two military supervisors were fixed.

sentences.zh: 並朝廷選差，其內侍幹當官並罷。」

translations.literal: All were selected and assigned by the court, and the inner-attendant managing officials were all abolished."
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed by the court, and the inner-attendant managers were abolished."

sentences.zh: 分案四，置吏八。

translations.literal: There were four sections and eight clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The directorate had four sections and eight clerks.

sentences.zh: 所隸官屬五：文思院，掌造金銀、犀玉工巧之物，金采、繪素裝鈿之飾，以供輿輦、冊寶、法物凡器服之用。

translations.literal: Its subordinate offices numbered five: the Literary Refinement Court, which managed manufacture of gold, silver, rhinoceros horn, and jade craft objects, and gold filigree, painted silk, and inlay ornament, to supply carriages and palanquins, seals and registers, ritual objects, and all accoutrements and garments.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw five subordinate offices. The Literary Refinement Court made gold, silver, rhinoceros horn, and jade craftwork, gold filigree, painted silk, and inlay ornament for carriages, seals and registers, ritual objects, and court accoutrements.

sentences.zh: 綾錦院，掌織紝錦繡，以供乘輿凡服飾之用。

translations.literal: The Damask and Brocade Court managed weaving of damask and embroidery to supply all imperial carriage garments and adornments.
translations.idiomatic: The Damask and Brocade Court wove damask and embroidery for all imperial dress and adornment.

sentences.zh: 染院，掌染絲枲幣帛。

translations.literal: The Dyeing Court managed dyeing of silk, hemp, and silks and cloths.
translations.idiomatic: The Dyeing Court dyed silk, hemp, and fabrics.

sentences.zh: 裁造院，掌裁制服飾。

translations.literal: The Cutting and Tailoring Court managed cutting and making garments and adornments.
translations.idiomatic: The Cutting and Tailoring Court cut and made garments and adornments.

sentences.zh: 文繡院，掌纂繡，以供乘輿服御及賓客祭祀之用，

translations.literal: The Literary Embroidery Court managed embroidery to supply imperial carriage accoutrements and the needs of guests and sacrifices,
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Embroidery Court produced embroidery for imperial use and for guests and sacrifices,

sentences.zh: 〈（崇寧三年置，招繡工三百人。）〉
